---
title: Reproducibility
description: Layouts, seeds and threads, and when results are bit-for-bit reproducible.
jupyter: python3
---

polars-umap can reproduce two versions of the umap-learn pipeline, selected with `layout`.

| | `layout="0.6"` (default) | `layout="0.5"` |
|---|---|---|
| Reproduces | umap-learn 0.6 with `optimizer="adam"` | umap-learn 0.5 (and 0.6 defaults) |
| Initialization | recursive (graph coarsening, anchored on PCA) | spectral |
| Optimizer | Adam, with deterministic negative sampling | Hogwild SGD |
| Same seed, same result | yes, at any thread count | only with `n_threads=1` |
| Speed | faster | 2–3× slower on the CPU |

## Seeds

With the default layout, the same `random_state` gives exactly the same embedding, however many
threads you use:

```{python}
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from sklearn.datasets import load_digits

import polars_umap  # noqa: F401

X, _ = load_digits(return_X_y=True)
df = pl.DataFrame({"pixels": X})


def embed(**kwargs) -> np.ndarray:
    return df.select(pl.col("pixels").umap.fit_transform(**kwargs)).to_series().to_numpy()


a = embed(random_state=1)
b = embed(random_state=1, n_threads=2)
np.array_equal(a, b)
```

Without `random_state`, every run is different.

## The 0.5 layout

The 0.5 layout uses Hogwild SGD, where many threads update the embedding at once without locking.
That's fast, but the order of updates differs between runs, so the result does too, even with a
seed. The quality doesn't change. For an exact repeat, use a single thread:

```{python}
np.array_equal(
    embed(random_state=1, layout="0.5", n_threads=1),
    embed(random_state=1, layout="0.5", n_threads=1),
)
```

## Across versions

Results are reproducible for a given version of polars-umap. A new version may change them,
for example when the upstream implementation improves. Pin the version when exact reproducibility
over time matters.
